newsitem.title: POLAND: Zloty recaptures key resistance, awaits NBP action.
newsitem.headline: Zloty recaptures key resistance, awaits NBP action.

text.p: The Polish zloty again pushed above the key 1.5 percent from parity level in early Tuesday trade and the market waited for a National Bank of Poland (NBP) intervention to push the zloty back down below resistance.
Dealers said the zloty, propelled upward by foreign buying of Polish treasuries as well as other inflows, would probably remain bullish as the market had a surplus of currencies.
"(Currency) selling continues today...and players expect the central bank to act to reestablish resistance later in the session," said Tomasz Wolosz, forex dealer at BRE SA.
Dealers estimated that on Monday the central bank bought $45 million to keep the zloty from firming past 1.5 percent.
At 0850 GMT the zloty was quoted at 1.55/1.53 percent from the parity rate, up from opening's 1.49/1.45 percent from parity and Monday's close at 1.53/1.49 percent.
It was at 3.2430/40 to the dollar, down from opening's 3.2415/30 and at 1.8689/91 to the mark, up from 1.8725/35, in line with the U.S. currency's rise against the German unit.
Some expected the central bank to refrain from currency buying until late in Tuesday's session to lower its costs as trading volume often falls in the afternoon.
On the money market one-day rates inched up at offer after the NBP announced a 600 million zloty reverse repo and a 150 million NBP-bill sale, dealers said.
At 0905 GMT overnight rates were at 21.55/22.00 percent, up from 21.60/21.80 percent at opening and tomorrow/next rates were at 21.70/22.00 percent, against Monday's 21.85/22.05.
The treasury said on Monday that it will offer 600 million zlotys of 52-week T-bills at an additional primary auction on Wednesday. The value date for this tender is Friday, June 20.
